label: March 1916
headline: Snow on Lake Naroch
deck: Russia attacks in the thaw to draw German divisions from Verdun
caption: Russian infantry wade through melting snow towards German wire
body: On 18 March, answering France's call for help at Verdun, the Russian armies attack near Lake Naroch, among the marshes and woods east of Vilna. The bombardment is heavy but blind, the German positions are little hurt, and the infantry go forward in close order.

Then the thaw comes. The frozen ground turns to slush and water, men sink to the knee, and the attacks are made again and again for ten days. Russia loses some 100,000 men; in April the Germans win back most of the ground.
At Verdun the battle has spread to the left bank of the Meuse, where German attacks since 6 March aim at the ridges from which French guns fire across the river.
On 9 March Germany declares war on Portugal, which has seized the German ships in her harbours; Portuguese troops are to be sent to France.
briefs: Admiral von Tirpitz resigns as head of the German navy
A raid by Pancho Villa on New Mexico brings US troops into Mexico
Italy opens a fifth battle on the Isonzo to aid Verdun
